description: Test your knowledge of Gametogenesis and fertilization.

cards.text: What is the normal length of the menstrual cycle and how is it counted?
cards.answer: The average menstrual cycle is 28 days (normal range 21-35 days), counted from day 1 of menstrual bleeding to the day before the next period begins.

cards.text: What hormonal changes trigger the menstrual phase and what happens to the endometrium?
cards.answer: Degeneration of the corpus luteum causes sharp decline in oestrogen and progesterone. This leads to spiral artery vasoconstriction, endometrial ischaemia, necrosis of the functional layer, and shedding as menstrual flow.

tip.tip: No CL → No hormones → Ischaemia → Shedding

cards.text: Why does menstrual blood remain fluid rather than clotting?
cards.answer: Menstrual blood contains fibrinolysins released from endometrial tissue, which dissolve clots and prevent normal coagulation, allowing fluid flow.

cards.text: How much does the endometrium thicken during the proliferative phase?
cards.answer: The endometrium grows from approximately 1 mm at the end of menstruation to 3-4 mm by ovulation under oestrogen stimulation.

cards.text: What is the total duration of spermatogenesis from spermatogonia to mature spermatozoa?
cards.answer: Spermatogenesis takes approximately 64-74 days from the initial spermatogonial division to the release of mature spermatozoa.

tip.tip: 64-74 days = roughly 2 months of continuous production

cards.text: What are the three phases of spermatogenesis in order?
cards.answer: Spermatogonial phase (mitotic divisions producing primary spermatocytes), Meiotic phase (meiosis I and II producing spermatids), and Spermiogenesis (morphological transformation into mature spermatozoa).

cards.text: List four major morphological changes during spermiogenesis.
cards.answer: Nuclear condensation with histone replacement by protamines, acrosome formation from the Golgi apparatus, flagellum development from the centriole, and mitochondrial sheath formation around the midpiece.

cards.text: What is the clinical significance of blood clots in menstrual flow?
cards.answer: Presence of menstrual clots indicates heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia) that exceeds the fibrinolytic capacity of the endometrium, suggesting possible pathology.
